main_text.p: Meminerunt huius Legi. Grammatici, Helychius: [illegible, ~60 letters]
[illegible, ~80 letters] Iuse narrat Vaticana Prouerbiorum Appen-dix Centuria I. Proverbio LXXXII. [illegible, ~60 letters]
[illegible, ~60 letters] [?] Aprolius Centuria VIII. Proverbio XXV. [illegible, ~50 letters]

Icaque aedis profanata, quam nemo Diis supplicandi causa adit, indicium est, in illa mejere, aut ventrem exonerare: quod e verbis Sacerdotis Iouis Su-teris apud Aristophanem Plutonem, colligere est in promptu:
Ad haec adlufit Perfius Satyra I.
main_text.l: Pinge duos angues: pueri, facer est locus: extra
main_text.p: Plutarchus de Chrysippo loquens ex emendatione viri magni, [illegible, ~120 letters] Quare bonae illae merces apud Iuuenalem Satyra VI. ad aram Pudicitiae meinnt, quia omnem illum, quam a se longe amandabant, religionem atque cultum sublatum vel-icnt:
main_text.l: I nunc, & dubita, qua forbeat aura fanna
Tullia, quod nota dicat Collacia Maura,
Maura Pudicitia veterem cum praterit aram,
Noctibus hic ponunt lectica, minctluriunt hic,

page.notes: Much of this page is badly faded and blurred, especially the Greek lines and the first lines of the text. I could not read most of the Greek letter by letter, so those lines are marked illegible with approximate letter counts; I did not guess them. Latin passages near the middle and bottom are legible and are copied as printed. The name "Helychius" and the Latin word "Iuse" at the start of the Vaticana passage are doubtful. The word "meinnt" and the verse line "Tullia" are as printed. The Latin verse lines are copied as printed. No page number, catchword or signature is visible.
